rationale: Since lt ≈ lct + long-term claims, NEG(dltt/lt) is close to a monotone transform of the archive's +lct/lt leg, so this is effectively the sign-flipped mirror of "Near Term Obligation Wall Value" (which already reported a −5.1% alpha at t=−4.17) rather than a new measurement, and re-running a known result with the sign reversed is archive mining, not a falsifiable new mechanism.

This is a recombination of two already-evaluated legs — the archive's ebitda/lt coverage rank and the sign-flipped lct/lt composition effect re-expressed as dltt/lt — and averaging a leg with a slope-but-no-alpha profile against a leg whose alpha is a known sign flip is unlikely to isolate any new economic content.

The construct is thoughtfully decomposed (operating vs. interest-bearing liability growth) and the certification story is coherent, but growth in non-debt operating liabilities is the liability side of the working-capital accrual anomaly with exactly the predicted sign, and the proposal explicitly rules out external financing while never addressing accruals; it also openly reverse-engineers the residual of the archive's "Balance Sheet Repair" result.

Cash-to-current-liabilities is a genuine stock-of-liquidity dimension not yet tested in this archive, the expression matches the hypothesis and expected sign cleanly, and pairing it with the EBITDA yield is a defensible attempt to escape the FF5-spanned profitable-value corner — though cash holdings are themselves a documented positive return predictor, so the incremental content over that literature is modest.

This swaps a single operator (cross-sectional RANK to 5-period TS_RANK) on the distress leg of the already-evaluated "Debt Capacity Coverage Value" — a cosmetic variant by the stated criteria — and a 5-observation annual TS_RANK is too coarse to reliably distinguish cyclical from permanent coverage in any case.

Δceq minus Δre is, by construction, net external equity issuance, so the signal is a direct rediscovery of the well-documented net share issuance / composite issuance anomaly (largely spanned by CMA in the FF5 benchmark) merely interacted with book-to-market, and the reasoning's claim that it avoids "needing an issuance variable" mislabels what the expression actually computes.
